title: Wren and the Songbook
premise: Mirabel Oyelaran, a pastry chef drowning in debt and hiding from the family that disowned him, is snowed in at a failing vineyard inn with Odile Marchetti, the woman who broke his heart a decade ago, and her business partner-fiancé Theo. Trapped together over one long winter week, old wounds reopen: Mirabel discovers his late mother's songbook was sold to the vineyard's owner, tying his past to the very land now threatening his future. As thaw approaches, Mirabel must choose between a buyout offer that would erase the vineyard—and his mother's memory—or betting everything on a harvest festival that could save both the inn and himself. He forgives the man in the mirror, chooses Odile not as a second chance but as a first honest one, and the first harvest comes in just as his café reopens its doors.
about_author: Ulyana Fairweather is a former line cook who writes love stories set in kitchens, vineyards, and other places where people feed each other what they can't say aloud. She lives above her own tiny bakery with two opinionated cats and a sourdough starter older than her marriage.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A bank letter arrives at Sugarwren Café the same morning health inspector Odile Marchetti walks in—his ex, ten years gone, now engaged to a vineyard developer. The emotional beat is dread sharpened by recognition; Mirabel realizes his carefully invisible life is about to be seen.

chapters.title: The Road to Verrazzano Vineyards
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile drags Mirabel to the vineyard to cater a make-or-break investor dinner, guilt riding shotgun. The storm hits early; roads close; the investor never comes. The beat is reluctant proximity—two people who know each other's coffee orders but not each other anymore.

chapters.title: Snowbound with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Stranded with Odile and her fiancé Theo, Mirabel finds a handwritten songbook in the inn's parlor—his mother's handwriting, sold off during the worst year of his life. The beat is grief resurfacing; he bakes all night to keep from shattering.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses the vineyard is insolvent and his investor plan requires selling the estate—including the songbook archive—to a hotel chain. The beat is complicity and shame; Theo sees how much Mirabel loves Odile still, and hates that it clarifies things.

chapters.title: Flour and Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A power outage forces Mirabel and Odile to bake by firelight; she finally explains why she left—a pregnancy she ended alone, believing he'd have chosen his family's approval over her. The beat is raw honesty; the decade of silence cracks open.

chapters.title: The Songbook's Last Owner
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The innkeeper reveals Mirabel's estranged father sold the songbook to cover Mirabel's culinary school debt—the sacrifice he never knew about. The beat is vertigo; the villain of his story was paying for his dreams all along.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Roads open; Theo leaves to salvage the deal, asking Odile to come. She stays one more day instead, and they almost kiss before Mirabel pulls back, convinced he ruins everything he touches. The beat is fear wearing the mask of nobility.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel drives home through melting snow, confronts his father at last, and reads his mother's final song—an apology to herself for hiding. The beat is reckoning; he realizes invisibility was the price he paid to survive, and survival isn't the same as living.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the harvest festival, Mirabel proposes using his café's remaining credit to co-sign the vineyard's rescue, Odile leverages her inspector's report to block the hotel sale, and Theo—choosing friendship over pride—withdraws his bid. The beat is collective courage; found family forms out of former rivals.

chapters.title: Sugarwren, Reopened
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Spring: the café reopens with vineyard pastries on the menu, the songbook framed behind the counter, and Odile moving her boxes in—not a second chance, Mirabel decides, but the first honest one. The beat is quiet joy; staying visible turns out to be the sweetest risk he ever took.
